h1: Chaloklum Bay Resort — beachfront bungalows with a sea-facing pool on the quiet north coast
intro: If you want to escape the buzz of Thong Sala and Haad Rin for a quiet beach on the island's north coast — Chaloklum Bay Resort is a 3-star beach resort of around 30 bungalows, right on Chaloklum Bay, a fishing village that still feels simple and laid-back · The draw is that the bungalows sit around a sea-facing pool, a few steps from a white-sand beach with a reef close to shore, with free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free parking and a spa · It starts from around ฿1,500/night in normal season · But to be straight from the real reviews: the location and beach are the real deal, while room upkeep and service are things to read up on carefully before you book.

body.html: Chaloklum Bay Resort is a 3-star beach resort of around 30 bungalows at the western end of Chaloklum Bay (Chalok Lam), a fishing village on the north coast of Koh Phangan · What sets it apart from in-town stays is that it's genuinely beachfront, with bungalows set around an outdoor, sea-facing pool and a white-sand beach with a reef close to shore just a few steps away · Many reviews say the bay view at sunset and the easygoing fishing-village feel are exactly why they chose this side of the island in the first place.

Rooms come as a range of bungalows, from a Standard Bungalow and Garden Villa up to a Superior Seaview, a two-bedroom Family Bungalow and a Honeymoon Suite · Most are AC bungalows with a fridge, a balcony or patio and a sitting area separate from the bed · The reviews that like it say the bungalows are roomier than expected and you get a beachfront setting at a price that's still reasonable · But to be honest, a fair number of reviews flag the room condition — damp, peeling walls, deferred maintenance and cleanliness that isn't consistent across all the bungalows · It's worth asking to see the room first, and choosing a more recently refreshed type if one is offered.

"Beautiful, quiet beach and a pool facing the sea — you can sit and watch the sunset all evening, and the free breakfast was fine. But the room was older than I expected, so you have to accept some wear for the price."

The north-coast location is both the strength and the catch in one · Chaloklum Bay is quiet and calm, with none of the party scene of Haad Rin — good for genuine downtime, with several beachside seafood spots in the village to walk to, and it's a launch point for boats to Koh Ma and snorkelling over the reef · But understand that it's around 15–20 minutes by car from Thong Sala Pier and the main shops, on roads that wind over hills in places · Without your own wheels you'll be relying on the island's pricey taxis, so renting a scooter or car is the way to go if you plan to see other beaches.

There's a fair bit to be straight about, and it's why the overall scores here aren't high · Beyond the room condition and upkeep, plenty of reviews mention inconsistent front-desk service — some guests find the staff helpful, others get a cool welcome · A few reviews describe overbooking and being moved to another property, plus Wi-Fi charges that didn't match what was advertised, and patchy cleanliness of the beach and pool at times · The overall picture: TripAdvisor sits around 2.8 out of 5 (near the bottom of the island), while some platforms like Expedia/Hotels.com sit around 6 out of 10 — the wide spread shows the experience really depends on which bungalow you get and when you visit.

So who's it for? · It suits travellers who weight a quiet north-coast beachfront and price above all and can accept that rooms aren't new and service isn't slick · If you want to fall asleep to the waves, wake up and swim in a sea-facing pool, walk to seafood in a fishing village and aren't expecting a luxury resort — this delivers that mood for less than the big resorts on the east coast · But if you're after pristine rooms and dependable service, look instead at higher-scoring resorts around Haad Yao, Srithanu or Thong Nai Pan.

A tip from reading the real reviews: ask for a Seaview or a more recently refreshed bungalow, and inspect it before you accept — if you find damp walls or a musty smell, ask to switch right away · Book a free-cancellation rate in case plans change · Rent a car or scooter so you can get into town and reach other beaches · In the evening, walk to the village seafood spots in Chaloklum, and if you like snorkelling, ask the resort about trips to nearby Koh Ma.

highlights.title: Right on quiet Chaloklum Bay
highlights.text: Bungalows on a white-sand beach with a reef close to shore, in a calm fishing village — no Haad Rin party scene, just genuine downtime on the north coast.

highlights.title: A sea-facing pool
highlights.text: Bungalows set around an outdoor pool that faces the bay — sit and watch the sunset from the poolside, with free breakfast, free Wi-Fi and free parking.

highlights.title: Beachfront on a light budget
highlights.text: Beachfront bungalows from around ฿1,500/night in normal season — cheaper than the big east-coast resorts, for travellers who value location and price over a brand-new room.

honestSummary: Chaloklum Bay Resort stands out for its quiet, beachfront setting on the north coast and a sea-facing pool, at a price that's still light — ideal for travellers escaping the buzz for a simple fishing village · Just accept, as the real reviews show, that many bungalows are older and damp, upkeep and service are inconsistent, and it's far from town; ask to see the room first and have your own wheels.
honestChecks: If you expect pristine rooms and dependable service — many reviews report damp, peeling walls and inconsistent service → inspect the room first, choose a Seaview/refreshed type, or consider higher-scoring resorts around Haad Yao, Srithanu or Thong Nai Pan.
If you have no vehicle and want to walk to the pier and shops — Chaloklum is around 15–20 minutes by car from Thong Sala on winding roads → rent a scooter/car, or pick a stay in Thong Sala instead.
If you came for nightlife and a party vibe — the north coast is very quiet, with no Haad Rin scene → for the Full Moon Party, stay around Haad Rin or Ban Tai instead.

tips.title: Always ask to see the room first
tips.body: Several reviews report damp or musty bungalows — ask for a Seaview or a more recently refreshed room, check the condition before checking in, and ask to switch if it's not right.

tips.title: Rent a car or scooter
tips.body: Chaloklum is around 15–20 minutes by car from Thong Sala on winding roads — your own wheels make getting into town and over to Haad Yao or Srithanu far easier, and you skip the pricey island taxis.

tips.title: Eat seafood in the fishing village
tips.body: Chaloklum is a fishing village with several beachside seafood spots within walking distance — head out in the evening for fresh fish right by the water.

tips.title: Ask about Koh Ma and snorkelling
tips.body: Chaloklum Bay is the launch point for boats to Koh Ma, with a shallow reef you can snorkel — ask the resort about trips or a boat hire before planning your day.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Chaloklum Bay Resort Koh Phangan

faq.q: Where is Chaloklum Bay Resort and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's at 68/1 Moo 7 on Chaloklum Bay (Chalok Lam) on the north coast of Koh Phangan · It's a beachfront resort in a fishing village · It's around 15–20 minutes by car from Thong Sala Pier on roads that wind over hills in places · Without your own vehicle you'll rely on pricey island taxis, so renting a scooter or car is recommended.

faq.q: How much does Chaloklum Bay Resort cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: In normal season it starts at around ฿1,500/night for a Garden Villa · There's also a Standard Bungalow, a Superior Seaview and a two-bedroom Family Bungalow · Most are AC bungalows with a fridge and balcony · Prices swing with the season and full-moon nights, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is Chaloklum Bay Resort beachfront, and does it have a pool?
faq.a: Yes · It's a beachfront resort on Chaloklum Bay with an outdoor, sea-facing swimming pool · The bungalows sit around the pool, a few steps from a white-sand beach with a reef close to shore · There's free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, free parking and a spa.

faq.q: What are the reviews like, and what should I watch out for?
faq.a: Opinion splits clearly · The fans praise the quiet, lovely beach and the sea-facing pool · The critics flag older rooms, damp and peeling walls, and inconsistent service · TripAdvisor sits around 2.8/5 while some platforms sit around 6/10 · It's worth asking to see the room first and booking a free-cancellation rate.

faq.q: Who is Chaloklum Bay Resort best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a quiet north-coast beach at a light price and can accept that rooms aren't new · Good if you like a fishing-village feel, walking to seafood and swimming in a sea-facing pool · It's not for those wanting pristine rooms, dependable service, or a Haad Rin party vibe.

faq.q: What's there to do near Chaloklum Bay Resort?
faq.a: Within walking distance you have Chaloklum Beach and the village's beachside seafood spots · Nearby is the boat launch for Koh Ma, with a shallow reef you can snorkel, and boats on to Bottle Beach · With a vehicle, the west-coast beaches of Haad Yao and Srithanu aren't far.
